rows.note: 0.1 mg/kg x 1000 = 100 ug/kg total arsenic; 'named vegetable oils' (CXS 210-1999) fall under the CXS 193 'Edible fats and oils' ML, which names CXS 210-1999 as a relevant commodity standard. Register note attributes the number to CXS 210 s.5.1 / CXS 19 s.4; in the 2019-revision text CXS 210 s.5 carries no numeric ML and defers to CXS 193, so the operative citation should be CXS 193-1995. The current CXS 210 edition (2023/2024 amendments, which per FAO's history listing touched sections 2, 3, 4, 7.2, 8 and the Appendix, not s.5) could not be opened directly. Aside for the register: CXS 193 (2025) lead ML for edible fats and oils is 0.08 mg/kg, not the 0.1 mg/kg stated in the row note (not this row's analyte).

rows.note: 100 mg/kg x 1000 = 100000 ug/kg. In force since 2025-02-08, superseding GB 2760-2014. All three scope elements in the row (baked foods 07.0, deep-fried flour products 06.03.02.05, batter/breading/frying powder 06.11) carry the identical ≤100 mg/kg dry-basis Al residue condition. Caveat on framing: the instrument expresses this as a residue condition attached to the permitted alum additives (INS 522/523), not as a free-standing contaminant ML for aluminium from all sources; the row note's 'additive-agnostic total-aluminium residue cap' is the register's reading, defensible because the limit is on aluminium residue in the finished food, but it is not the instrument's own wording. Not verified from primary text: the register note's claims about the 2014 INS 541 ban and the Codex GSFA corroboration.
